title: Filled channel contract v1
description: THE CHANNEL CONTRACT IS A FORM, AND A STATION RUN FILLS IT IN. There is one document, not two: the channel's contract states the demand — every value the channel requires, and the carriage terms an entry must meet to be admitted — and a station run returns that same document with a proof column added to each row. Founder rulings on Vexa-ai/vexa-delivery#12, 2026-08-29. A filled instance therefore carries the SAME contract_id as the demand it answers, and binds itself to the exact bytes of that demand through fills_contract.sha256; the demand is constant across a channel, and what varies per set is the proof column. A CONTRACT BELONGS TO A CHANNEL, never to a release train and never to a station. Stations — staging, prod — are enforcement points of their channel's contract, not owners of contracts of their own, which is why `station` below is an attribution on the instance rather than a scope on the demand. Each train yields one filled instance per set. NOT YET EVALUATED BY THE VERIFIER. This schema is the definition the in-cluster verifier learns to read in turn 2; as of turn 1 (2026-08-29) it defines the document and validates instances offline, and the gate still admits entries on the carriage block alone. The evidence kind carried in a channel entry stays the string `validation_contract` this turn for schema compatibility with entries already published — the name is legacy, the document is the filled contract.

contract_id.description: The SAME id as the unfilled demand this instance answers. Not a derived or per-run id: a filled contract that renamed itself could not be matched back to the demand it claims to satisfy.

fills_contract.description: The binding to the unfilled demand, by BYTES and not by name. An id says what a document calls itself; the drift that matters keeps the id and moves a threshold, so the hash is the load-bearing half. It is the sha256 of the contract record's bytes exactly as they sit in the stations ledger — no re-serialisation, no dropped trailing newline.

channel.description: The channel whose contract this is. Optional because it is derivable from contract_id in every case shipped so far, and stated when a reader would otherwise have to derive it.

station.description: WHICH ENFORCEMENT POINT FILLED THIS IN — the station name, e.g. `vexa-staging-bbb` or `vexa-prod`. A station does not own a contract; it answers its channel's. An unattributable filled contract looks like proof and is not, which is the same reason --verdict-out refuses to write a verdict with no --station.

release.description: The release the set under test carried, e.g. `0.12.23-estate-20260829`. Optional: a filled contract is about the SET, and the entry reference below names it precisely.

entry_ref.description: The channel entry whose set this instance proves, e.g. `channel.vexa.ai/vexa/channel/vexa-internal:0.12.23-estate-20260829-seq6`.

at.description: When the fill completed. Individual rows may carry their own filled_at when they were proven at different times.

verdict.description: THE BOTTOM LINE, and it is a judgement about the rows below rather than a separate finding. ELIGIBLE means every row whose enforcement is `required` is proven. NOT_ELIGIBLE means at least one required row is not. INCOMPLETE is the honest third answer: the run ended with required rows neither proven nor refuted — a station that could not reach a dependency, a smoke that was never attempted — and it exists so that such a run cannot be recorded as either a pass or a failure.

filled_by.description: The tool or operator that performed the fill, for provenance. Not an authorisation: nothing here is signed, and a filled contract is signed as an attestation subject if it is signed at all.

carriage.description: The carriage terms carried through from the demand, VERBATIM. Copied rather than referenced so the filled instance is readable standing alone, and checkable against fills_contract.sha256 by anyone who has the record. These are terms on the ENTRY that carries the set — publication mode, evidence kinds, sequence floor — not claims about the software, which is why they carry no proof column.

required_values.description: THE FORM, ROW BY ROW. Every row of the demand appears here, in the demand's own order, whether or not it was proven — a filled contract that omitted the rows it could not answer would read as complete while being silently narrower than the contract it claims to fill.

id.description: The demand's own row id, e.g. `V-est-3`. Unchanged from the unfilled contract.

claim.description: The demand's own words for what must be true, carried through unchanged. Restating it in the filler's words is how a row quietly becomes a weaker row.

rank.description: How the claim can be established at all: by a machine check, by a population over a window, or only by a person.

validation.description: How the demand says this row is to be proven, carried through unchanged.

enforcement.description: Whether an unproven row blocks. Carried through from the demand; a filler may not soften it.

proof.description: THE COLUMN THE STATION ADDS, and the only part of a row a fill may write. Absent means the row was not reached at all by this run, which is different from `not-run` — absent is silence, `not-run` is a stated decision with a reason.

status.description: `proven` — the claim was established, and `evidence` points at what establishes it. `unproven` — the run attempted the claim and it did not hold; this is a finding, and `notes` says what was observed. `not-run` — the run did not attempt it, and `notes` says why. THE THREE ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE: recording a not-run row as unproven manufactures a failure, and recording it as proven is the failure this whole document exists to prevent.

evidence.description: What a reader opens to check the row for themselves. Required in practice for a `proven` row — a proof with no pointer is an assertion — and useful on the other two.

pointer.description: Where the evidence is: a path inside the station report bundle, an OCI reference, or a URL. Resolvable by someone who is not the author.

sha256.description: The evidence bytes' hash, where the evidence is a file. Without it a pointer names a location whose contents can change after the claim was made.

note.description: What this particular artifact shows, when the pointer alone does not say.

environment.description: WHERE THIS WAS PROVEN, because the same claim proven in two places is worth two different amounts. The station's own cluster identity — `bbb k3s, single node, namespace vexa-station-seq6` — not merely `staging`.

fidelity.description: EVERY STAND-IN THE PROOF LEANED ON. Real by default; a double is permitted where real is impossible or harmful, and it carries its justification. An unjustified double is a contract violation, not a shortcut — and a row proven against doubles nobody listed is the most expensive kind of green there is.

dependency.description: What was stood in for, e.g. `postgres`, `stripe`, `transcription`.

kind.description: `real` — the production-shaped dependency itself. `double` — a stand-in. `absent` — not present at all, so anything downstream of it was not exercised.

justification.description: Why a double or an absence was the right call here. Required by the rule, not by the schema, so that a missing justification is visible as an empty string rather than an omitted key.

does_not_prove.description: THE SCOPE LIMIT, IN THE FILLER'S OWN WORDS, ON THE ROW ITSELF. What a reader might reasonably take from this row that it does not actually support — the assert ran against a locally built image rather than the published digest; the deployments came up against a placeholder billing key. This is the field that stops a green row being read as more than it is, and it is inline on the row because a caveat kept anywhere else is a caveat nobody reads at the moment they are reading the row.

notes.description: What was observed. On an `unproven` row this is the finding; on a `not-run` row it is the reason.

filled_at.description: When THIS row was established, where rows were proven at different times — a soak row filled over a window, a human row signed days later.

filled_by.description: The station that filled this row, where a single instance aggregates rows from more than one enforcement point.
